__setting_1.label: Early Makkah · ~610 CE
__setting_1.context: Revealed in the earliest years of the Prophetic mission in Makkah (~610–612 CE), when the community of believers was small and largely from among the weak and marginalized. The Quraysh had begun to mock and ostracize the Muslims, but open persecution had not yet begun.

__setting_2.label: 1 AH · 622 CE · Madinah
__setting_2.context: Revealed in Madinah during the early Medinan period (1–3 AH / 622–624 CE), when the Muslim community was being established for the first time as a political and social entity. The Prophet drafted the Constitution of Madinah, the direction of prayer (qibla) was changed to Makkah, and the Battle of Badr — the first major military engagement — took place.

2:115.occasion: And to Allah belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn (yourselves or your faces) there is the Face of Allah (and He is High above, over His Throne). Surely, Allah is Sufficient (for His creatures' needs), Knowing (115) Facing the Qiblah (Direction of the Prayer) This ruling brought comfort to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions, who were driven out of Makkah and had to depart from the area of Al-Masjid Al-Haram. 2:158.occasion: The Ansar, who in the time of Jahiliyyah used to enter the state of Ihram for the idol Manat at Mushallal, felt hesitant about going (performing Sa'i) between As-Safa and Al-Marwah after Islam. They asked the Messenger of Allah about this, and the verse was revealed affirming that As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.
2:158.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:185.occasion: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind and clear proofs for the guidance and the criterion (between right and wrong). So whoever of you sights (the crescent on the first night of) the month (of Ramadan, i.e., is present at his home), he must observe Sawm (fasting) that month, and whoever is ill or on a journey, the same number [of days which one did not observe Sawm (fasting) must be made up] from other days. Allah intends for you ease, and He does not want to make things difficult for you.

2:187.occasion: In early Islam, food, drink, and relations with one's wife were forbidden after one slept or prayed the 'Isha prayer. Qays bin Sirmah al-Ansari, worn out from working his land, fell asleep before eating and fainted from hunger the next day, and others such as 'Umar also fell into this difficulty. The verse was then revealed permitting eating, drinking, and intimacy throughout the night until the dawn appears.
2:187.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:189.occasion: People asked the Messenger of Allah about the crescent moons, so the verse was revealed explaining that they are time-markers for the worship, the waiting periods of women, and the Hajj of mankind. The remainder of the verse was revealed because the Ansar used to enter their houses from the back rather than through the front doors when returning from a journey, considering this a form of piety.
2:189.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:195.occasion: It was revealed concerning the Ansar who, after Islam became strong and victorious, privately resolved among themselves to return to their long-neglected estates, families, and properties and to give up Jihad. The verse clarified that abandoning the cause of Allah, not fighting, is the true self-destruction.
2:195.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:196.occasion: Ka'b bin 'Ujrah was brought to the Prophet while in Ihram with lice falling in great numbers over his face. The Prophet directed him to shave his head and pay a ransom by fasting three days, feeding six poor persons, or sacrificing a sheep. Ka'b said this ruling was revealed regarding his own case in particular, though it then applied to everyone in general.
2:196.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:198.occasion: There is no sin on you if you seek the bounty of your Lord (during pilgrimage by trading). Then when you leave 'Arafat, remember Allah (by glorifying His praises, i.e., prayers and invocations) at the Mash'ar-il-Haram. And remember Him (by invoking Allah for all good) as He has guided you, and verily you were before, of those who were astray (198) Commercial Transactions during Hajj Al-Bukhari reported that Ibn 'Abbas said, "Ukaz, Mijannah and Dhul-Majaz were trading posts during the time of Jahiliyyah. During that era, they did not like the idea of conducting business transactions during the Hajj season.

2:200.occasion: So when you have accomplished your Manasik, remember Allah as you remember your forefathers or with far more remembrance. But of mankind there are some who say: "Our Lord! Give us (Your bounties) in this world!" and for such there will be no portion in the Hereafter (200)And of them there are some who say: "Our Lord! Give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and save us from the torment of the Fire! (201)For them there will be alloted a share for what they have earned.

2:204.occasion: And of mankind there is he whose speech may please you (O Muhammad ﷺ), in this worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to that which is in his heart, yet he is the most quarrelsome of the opponents (204)And when he turns away (from you O Muhammad ), his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle, and Allah likes not mischief (205)And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah", he is led by arrogance to (more) crime. So enough for him is Hell, and worst indeed is that place to rest (206)And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah.

2:207.occasion: It was revealed about Suhayb bin Sinan ar-Rumi. When he became a Muslim in Makkah and wished to emigrate, the Quraysh would not let him leave with his wealth, so he gave up all his property to them and chose to migrate for the sake of Allah.
2:207.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:215.occasion: They ask you (O Muhammad ﷺ) what they should spend. Say: "Whatever you spend of good must be for parents and kindred and orphans and Al-Masakin (the poor) and the wayfarer, and whatever you do of good deeds, truly, Allah knows it well. (215) Who deserves the Nafaqah (Spending or Charity) Muqatil bin Hayyan said that this Ayah was revealed about the voluntary charity. The Ayah means, 'They ask you (O Muhammad ﷺ) how they should spend,' as Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid have stated.

2:217.occasion: It was revealed in connection with the expedition of 'Abdullah bin Jahsh, whose party fought and killed a man and took captives during a sacred month. When the disbelievers reproached the Muslims for fighting in the sacred month, the verse was revealed clarifying the matter, and the following verse gave the believers who had emigrated and striven hope of Allah's mercy.
2:217.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:218.occasion: They ask you concerning fighting in the Sacred Months. Say, "Fighting therein is a great (transgression) but a greater (transgression) with Allah is to prevent mankind from following the way of Allah, to disbelieve in Him, to prevent access to Al-Masjid Al-Haram (at Makkah), and to drive out its inhabitants, and Al-Fitnah is worse than killing." And they will never cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion (Islamic Monotheism) if they can. And whosoever of you turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever, then his deeds will be lost in this life and in the Hereafter, and they will be the dwellers of the Fire.

2:219.occasion: It was revealed as the first stage in the prohibition of intoxicants and gambling, after 'Umar bin al-Khattab supplicated, 'O Allah, give us a clear ruling regarding Al-Khamr.' Later verses in Surat An-Nisa' and Surat Al-Ma'idah completed the prohibition.
2:219.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:220.occasion: They ask you (O Muhammad ﷺ) concerning alcoholic drink and gambling. Say: "In them is a great sin, and (some) benefits for men, but the sin of them is greater than their benefit." And they ask you what they ought to spend. Say: "That which is (spare) beyond your needs." Thus Allah makes clear to you His Laws in order that you may give thought (219)In (to) this worldly life and in the Hereafter. And they ask you concerning orphans. Say: "The best thing is to work honestly in their property, and if you mix your affairs with theirs, then they are your brothers.

2:222.occasion: They ask you concerning menstruation. Say: "That is an Adha, therefore, keep away from women during menses and go not in unto them till they are purified." And when they have purified themselves, then go in unto them as Allah has ordained for you. Truly, Allah loves those who turn unto Him in repentance and loves those who purify themselves (222)Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth, when or how you will, and send (good deeds, or ask Allah to bestow upon you pious offspring) for your own selves beforehand.

2:223.occasion: The Jews used to claim that if a man approached his wife from behind, in the vagina, the resulting child would be born cross-eyed. After some of the Ansar also asked the Prophet about this, the verse was revealed declaring that wives are a tilth and that a man may approach his wife as he wishes so long as it is in the proper place.
2:223.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:229.occasion: Ibn Jarir reported that it was revealed concerning Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas and his wife, in the context of khul', where the wife sought release from the marriage by returning what she had been given.
2:229.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:230.occasion: The divorce is twice, after that either you retain her on reasonable terms or release her with kindness. And it is not lawful for you (men) to take back (from your wives) any of what you gave them (the Mahr, bridal-money given by the husband to his wife at the time of marriage), except when both parties fear that they would be unable to keep the limits ordained by Allah (e.g., to deal with each other on a fair basis). Then if you fear that they would not be able to keep the limits ordained by Allah, then there is no sin on either of them if she gives back (the Mahr or a part of it).

2:232.occasion: It was revealed about Ma'qil bin Yasar al-Muzani. His sister had been divorced by her husband, and after her waiting period ended the husband sought to remarry her and she was willing, but Ma'qil refused to allow it. The verse forbade guardians from preventing women from returning to their former husbands in such a case.
2:232.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:238.occasion: People used to speak to one another about their affairs during the prayer until this verse, commanding them to stand before Allah devoutly, was revealed, after which they were ordered to refrain from talking during the prayer.
2:238.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:239.occasion: Guard strictly (five obligatory) As-Salawat (the prayers) especially the Middle Salah.And stand before Allah with obedience (238)And if you fear (an enemy), (perform Salah) on foot or riding. And when you are in safety, then remember Allah (pray) in the manner He has taught you, which you knew not (before)(239) Allah commands that the prayer should be performed properly and on time.

2:246.occasion: Have you not thought about the group of the Children of Israel after (the time of) Musa? When they said to a Prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king and we will fight in Allah's way." He said, "Would you then refrain from fighting, if fighting was prescribed for you?" They said, "Why should we not fight in Allah's way while we have been driven out of our homes and our children (families have been taken as captives)?" But when fighting was ordered for them, they turned away, all except a few of them.

2:267.occasion: It was revealed about some of the Ansar who, when the date harvest came, would hang branches of dates in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah for the poor emigrants to eat, but some of them would mix in inferior, poor-quality dates among the good ones.
2:267.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:268.occasion: O you who believe! Spend of the good things which you have (legally) earned, and of that which We have produced from the earth for you, and do not aim at that which is bad to spend from it, (though) you would not accept it save if you close your eyes and tolerate therein. And know that Allah is Rich (free of all needs), and worthy of all praise (267)Shaytan threatens you with poverty and orders you to commit Fahsha' (evil deeds) whereas Allah promises you forgiveness from Himself and bounty, and Allah is All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Knower (268)He grants Hikmah to whom He wills, and he, to whom Hikmah is granted, is indeed gra…

2:272.occasion: Not upon you (Muhammad ﷺ) is their guidance, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend in good, it is for yourselves, when you spend not except seeking Allah's Face. And whatever you spend in good, it will be repaid to you in full, and you shall not be wronged (272)(Charity is) for Fuqara' (the poor), who in Allah's cause are restricted (from travel), and cannot move about in the land (for trade or work). The one who knows them not, thinks that they are rich because of their modesty. You may know them by their mark, they do not beg of people at all.

2:278.occasion: It was revealed concerning outstanding usurious dealings left over from the time of Jahiliyyah between Banu 'Amr bin 'Umayr of the tribe of Thaqif and Banu al-Mughirah of Makhzum. When both tribes embraced Islam, a dispute arose over paying the accumulated interest, the matter was referred to the Messenger of Allah, and the verse was revealed forbidding the taking of the remaining riba.
2:278.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:279.occasion: O you who believe! Have Taqwa of Allah and give up what remains from Riba, if you are (really) believers (278)And if you do not do it, then take a notice of war from Allah and His Messenger but if you repent,you shall have your capital sums. Deal not unjustly, and you shall not be dealt with unjustly (279)And if the debtor is having a hard time, then grant him time till it is easy for him to repay; but if you remit it by way of charity, that is better for you if you did but know (280)And have Taqwa the Day when you shall be brought back to Allah.

2:282.occasion: O you who believe! When you contract a debt for a fixed period, write it down. Let a scribe write it down in justice between you. Let not the scribe refuse to write, as Allah has taught him, so let him write. Let him (the debtor) who incurs the liability dictate, and he must have Taqwa of Allah, his Lord, and diminish not anything of what he owes. But if the debtor is of poor understanding, or weak, or is unable to dictate for himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And get two witnesses out of your own men.

2:284.occasion: To Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is able to do all things (284) Would the Servants be Accountable for What They Conceal in Their Hearts? Allah states that His is the kingship of the heavens and earth and of what and whoever is on or between them, that He has perfect watch over them. No apparent matter or secret that the heart conceals is ever a secret to Him, however minor it is.

2:285.occasion: The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and (so do) the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His Angels, His Books, and His Messengers. (They say,) "We make no distinction between one another of His Messengers ـ and they say, "We hear, and we obey. (We seek) Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return (of all). (285)Allah burdens not a person beyond his scope. He gets reward for that (good) which he has earned, and he is punished for that (evil) which he has earned.

__setting_3.label: 2 AH · 623 CE · Madinah
__setting_3.context: Revealed in Madinah during the early Medinan period (1–3 AH / 622–624 CE), when the Muslim community was being established for the first time as a political and social entity. The Prophet drafted the Constitution of Madinah, the direction of prayer (qibla) was changed to Makkah, and the Battle of Badr — the first major military engagement — took place.

3:1.occasion: The Tafsir of Surah Āl 'Imrān (Chapter 3) Surah Āl-'Imrān was revealed in Al-Madinah, as evident by the fact that the first eighty-three Ayat in it relate to the delegation from Najran that arrived in Al-Madinah on the ninth year of Hijrah (632 CE). We will elaborate on this subject when we explain the Ayah about the Mubahalah [3:61] in this Surah, Allah willing. We should also state that we mentioned the virtues of Surah Āl-'Imrān along with the virtues of Surat Al-Baqarah in the beginning of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Baqarah.

3:55.occasion: And (remember) when Allah said: "O 'Isa! I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify [save] you from those who disbelieve, and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve till the Day of Resurrection. Then you will return to Me and I will judge between you in the matters in which you used to dispute (55)"As to those who disbelieve, I will punish them with severe torment in this world and in the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers. (56)And as for those who believe and do righteous good deeds, Allah will pay them their reward in full.

Why do you disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah, while you bear witness. (70)"O People of the Scripture! Why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?

3:77.occasion: Al-Ash'ath bin Qays had a dispute with a Jewish man over a piece of land; the Jew denied his right and Al-Ash'ath had no evidence. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) called on the Jew to swear an oath, Al-Ash'ath feared he would swear falsely and seize the land, and this verse was revealed concerning that.
3:77.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:79.occasion: It is not (possible) for any human being to whom Allah has given the Book and Al-Hukm and prophethood to say to the people: "Be my worshippers rather than Allah's." On the contrary (he would say): "Be you Rabbaniyyun, because you are teaching the Book, and you are studying it. (79)Nor would he order you to take angels and Prophets for lords.

3:90.occasion: Some people embraced Islam, then disbelieved, then became Muslims again, and then reverted once more. They sent word inquiring about their case and the matter was put to the Prophet (peace be upon him), so this verse was revealed about those who increase in disbelief.
3:90.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:91.occasion: Verily, those who disbelieved after their belief and then went on increasing in their disbelief never will their repentance be accepted. And they are those who are astray (90)Verily, those who disbelieved, and died while they were disbelievers, the (whole) earth full of gold will not be accepted from anyone of them if they offered it as a ransom.

3:102.occasion: O you who believe! Have Taqwa of Allah as is His due, and die not except as (true) Muslims (102)And hold fast, all of you together, to the Rope of Allah, and be not divided among yourselves, and remember Allah's favor on you, for you were enemies of one another but He joined your hearts together, so that, by His grace, you became brethren, and you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it.

3:103.occasion: This verse about Allah uniting the hearts of the believers was revealed concerning the Aws and Khazraj, who had been bitter enemies engaged in long wars during the time of Jahiliyyah, until Allah joined their hearts through Islam and made them brothers.
3:103.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:113.occasion: These verses were revealed about the People of the Scripture who embraced Islam, such as 'Abdullah bin Salam, Asad bin 'Ubayd, Tha'labah bin Sa'yah and Usayd bin Sa'yah, distinguishing them from those of the People of the Book who were rebuked earlier.
3:113.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:122.occasion: This verse about the two parties who were about to lose heart was revealed concerning the two Muslim clans Bani Harithah and Bani Salamah at the battle of Uhud, of whom Allah said that He was their Protector.
3:122.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:168.occasion: This verse, describing those who stayed behind and said of their slain brethren that they would not have been killed had they listened, was revealed concerning 'Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, the chief of the hypocrites.
3:168.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:169.occasion: These verses about the martyrs being alive with their Lord were revealed concerning those killed at Uhud. Allah placed their souls in green birds wandering in Paradise, and when they wished their brethren could know their state, Allah said He would convey the news to them.
3:169.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_4.label: 3 AH · 624 CE · Madinah
__setting_4.context: Revealed in Madinah during the early Medinan period (1–3 AH / 622–624 CE), when the Muslim community was being established for the first time as a political and social entity. The Prophet drafted the Constitution of Madinah, the direction of prayer (qibla) was changed to Makkah, and the Battle of Badr — the first major military engagement — took place.

4:2.occasion: And give unto orphans their property and do not exchange (your) bad things for (their) good ones; and devour not their substance (by adding it) to your substance. Surely, this is a great sin (2)And if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry (other) women of your choice, two or three, or four; but if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly (with them), then only one or (the captives and the servants) that your right hands possess.

4:3.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from al-Bukhari that 'A'ishah said a man was the guardian of a female orphan and married her although he had no desire for her, mixing her wealth with his and withholding her share. This verse was revealed concerning his case, forbidding guardians from marrying their orphan wards unless they treated them justly and gave a fair dowry.
4:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:5.occasion: And give not unto the unwise your wealth which Allah has made a means of support for you, but feed and clothe them therewith, and speak to them words of kindness and justice (5)And test orphans until they reach the age of marriage; if then you find sound judgment in them, release their property to them, but consume it not wastefully and hastily, fearing that they should grow up. And whoever among guardians is rich, he should take no wages, but if he is poor, let him have for himself what is just and reasonable (according to his work).

This verse was revealed forbidding inheriting women against their will.

4:43.occasion: Ibn Kathir records that Sa'd narrated this verse was revealed after an Ansari man hosted a meal where the guests drank until intoxicated and boasted, and a man struck Sa'd's nose with a camel bone. He also cites 'Ali that 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf served wine at a meal, and when the intoxicated man led the prayer he misrecited Surat al-Kafirun, so the verse forbidding prayer while drunk was revealed.
4:43.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:58.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports it is well known, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj and 'Umar, that this verse on rendering back trusts was revealed concerning 'Uthman bin Talhah, from whom the Prophet took the key of the Ka'bah on the day Makkah was conquered; the Prophet then recited the verse and returned the key to him.
4:58.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:59.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites al-Bukhari from Ibn 'Abbas that this verse commanding obedience to those in authority was revealed about 'Abdullah bin Hudhafah bin Qays, whom the Messenger of Allah had sent in command of a military expedition.
4:59.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:65.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from al-Bukhari that az-Zubayr disputed with an Ansari man over irrigation water; when the Prophet judged in az-Zubayr's favor the Ansari accused him of partiality because az-Zubayr was his relative. Az-Zubayr said he believed this verse, swearing none truly believe until they accept the Prophet's judgment, was revealed concerning that case.
4:65.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

Jibril then brought this verse promising the obedient the company of the Prophets, and the Prophet sent the man the good news.

4:77.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf and companions came to the Prophet in Makkah saying they had been mighty as idolaters but became weak after believing, and he told them he was commanded to pardon and not to fight. After the move to al-Madinah they were commanded to fight, yet some held back, so this verse was revealed about those told to restrain their hands.
4:77.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:78.occasion: Have you not seen those who were told to hold back their hands (from fighting) and perform Salah and give Zakah, but when the fighting was ordained for them, behold! a section of them fear men as they fear Allah or even more. They say: "Our Lord! Why have You ordained for us fighting? Would that You granted us respite for a short period?" Say: "Short is the enjoyment of this world.

4:82.occasion: Do they not then consider the Qur'an carefully? Had it been from other than Allah, they would surely, have found therein contradictions in abundance (82)When there comes to them some matter touching (public) safety or fear, they make it known (among the people); if only they had referred it to the Messenger or to those charged with authority among them, the proper investigators would have understood it from them (directly).

4:83.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Muslim that when 'Umar heard a rumor circulating that the Messenger of Allah had divorced his wives, he went and asked the Prophet directly, who said he had not, after which 'Umar proclaimed the truth and this verse on properly investigating reports of safety or fear was revealed.
4:83.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:92.occasion: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake; and whosoever kills a believer by mistake, he must set free a believing slave and submit compensation (blood money) to the deceased's family unless they remit it. And whoso finds this beyond his means, he must fast for two consecutive months in order to seek repentance from Allah.

__setting_5.label: 9 AH · 630 CE · Madinah
__setting_5.context: Revealed in Madinah during the mature Medinan period (7–10 AH / 628–632 CE), as the Muslim state grew in strength. The conquest of Makkah (8 AH), the campaigns to the north, and the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH) all occurred in this period. The Quran was approaching completion.

5:2.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Zayd bin Aslam that at Al-Hudaybiyyah, after the idolators had prevented the Muslims from visiting the House, some idolators passed by from the east intending 'Umrah. The Companions said, 'Let us prevent these just as their fellows prevented us,' so Allah revealed the warning not to let hatred for a people lead them to transgression.
5:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:3.occasion: Forbidden to you (for food) are: Al-Maytah (the dead animals), blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been slaughtered as a sacrifice for other than Allah, and that which has been killed by strangling, or by a violent blow, or by a headlong fall, or by the goring of horns ـand that which has been (partly) eaten by a wild animal ـunless you are able to slaughter it (before its death) - and that which is sacrificed (slaughtered) on An-Nusub (stone altars). (Forbidden) also is to make decisions with Al-Azlam (arrows)(all) that is Fisq (disobedience and sin).

5:5.occasion: Made lawful to you this day are At-Tayyibat. The food of the People of the Scripture is lawful to you, and your food is lawful to them. (Lawful to you in marriage) are chaste women from the believers and chaste women from those who were given the Scripture before your time when you have given them their due, desiring chastity, not illegal sexual intercourse, nor taking them as girlfriends (or lovers).

5:11.occasion: Ibn Kathir mentions that Muhammad bin Ishaq, Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said this was revealed about Banu An-Nadir, who plotted to drop a stone on the Prophet's head when he came to them seeking help to pay blood money. Allah informed His Prophet of the plot and he returned safely to Al-Madinah, and this verse about Allah withholding their hands was sent down.
5:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:41.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Umar that two Jews, a man and a woman, committed adultery, and the Jews came to the Prophet seeking his judgment, having concealed the verse of stoning in the Tawrah, intending to follow him only if he ruled for flogging. The Prophet had the verse of stoning uncovered and ordered the two to be stoned, and these verses were revealed about them.
5:41.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:42.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that these verses concerned the blood money dispute between Bani An-Nadir and Bani Qurayzah, where the dead of An-Nadir received full blood money while Qurayzah received only half. They referred the matter to the Messenger of Allah, who made the blood money equal for both groups, and these verses were sent down.
5:42.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:43.occasion: (41. O Messenger! Let not those who hurry to fall into disbelief grieve you, of such who say, "We believe" with their mouths but their hearts have no faith. And of the Jews are men who listen much and eagerly to lies, listening to others who have not come to you. They change the words from their places; they say, "If you are given this, take it, but if you are not given this, then beware!" And whomsoever Allah wants to put in Fitnah, you can do nothing for him against Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah does not want to purify; for them there is a disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter a great torment.)(42.

5:49.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Muhammad bin Ishaq from Ibn 'Abbas that Jewish chiefs including Ka'b bin Asad, Ibn Saluba, 'Abdullah bin Surya and Shas bin Qays came to the Prophet offering to believe in him if he ruled in their favor in a dispute with their own people, hoping to misguide him from his religion. The Prophet refused, and these verses were revealed about them.
5:49.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

When the Prophet heard, he summoned them and declared that he himself fasts and breaks his fast, prays and sleeps, and marries women, and that whoever turns away from his Sunnah is not of him.

Then the verse prohibiting intoxicants and gambling was revealed.
5:90.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_6.label: Mid Makkah · ~617 CE
__setting_6.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

6:65.occasion: Jabir bin Abdullah reported that when this verse was revealed, mentioning torment sent from above and from beneath their feet, the Prophet (peace be upon him) sought refuge with Allah's Face from each; but when the warning of being thrown into confusion through party strife and tasting one another's violence was mentioned, he said this was lighter or easier.
6:65.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:93.occasion: Ikrimah and Qatadah stated that the verse condemning whoever invents a lie against Allah or falsely claims 'I have received inspiration' was revealed concerning Musaylimah the Liar, who falsely claimed to receive revelation.
6:93.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:94.occasion: And who can be more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah, or says: "I have received inspiration," whereas he is not inspired in anything; and who says, "I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed." And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, while the angels are stretching forth their hands (saying): "Deliver your souls! This day you shall be recompensed with the torment of degradation because of what you used to utter against Allah other than the truth. And you used to reject His Ayat with disrespect! (93)And truly you have come unto Us alone, as We created you the first time.

6:141.occasion: Ibn Jurayj reported that the command 'waste not by extravagance' was revealed concerning Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas, who, upon harvesting his date palms, resolved to feed everyone who came to him that day until he was left with no dates by evening.
6:141.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:142.occasion: And it is He Who produces gardens Ma'rushat and not Ma'rushat, and date palms, and crops of different shape and taste, and olives, and pomegranates, similar, and different. Eat of their fruit when they ripen, but pay the due thereof on the day of their harvest, and waste not by extravagance. Verily, He likes not the wasteful (141)And of the cattle (are some) for burden and (some smaller) for Farsh. Eat of what Allah has provided for you, and follow not the footsteps of Shaytan.

6:145.occasion: Say: "I find not in that which has been revealed to me anything forbidden to be eaten by one who wishes to eat it, unless it be Maytah (a dead animal) or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine; for that surely, is unclean (Rijs), or immorally slaughtered in the name of other than Allah. But whosoever is forced by necessity without willful disobedience, nor transgressing due limits; (for him) certainly, your Lord is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

6:156.occasion: Lest you should say: "The Book was sent down only to two sects before us, and for our part, we were in fact unaware of what they studied. __setting_7.label: Mid Makkah · ~615 CE
__setting_7.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

7:31.occasion: This verse was revealed concerning the idolaters who used to perform Tawaf around the Sacred House while naked, both men and women. Allah commanded them to take their adornment, meaning to wear proper clothes that cover the body, at every place of prayer.
7:31.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

7:187.occasion: The Quraysh repeatedly questioned the Prophet (peace be upon him) about the timing of the Last Hour, asking when it would come because they denied and discounted it. The Prophet kept being asked and kept mentioning the Hour until this verse was revealed, directing him to refer its knowledge to Allah alone.
7:187.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_8.label: 1 AH · 622 CE · Madinah
__setting_8.context: Revealed in Madinah during the early Medinan period (1–3 AH / 622–624 CE), when the Muslim community was being established for the first time as a political and social entity. The Prophet drafted the Constitution of Madinah, the direction of prayer (qibla) was changed to Makkah, and the Battle of Badr — the first major military engagement — took place.

8:27.occasion: In the year of the conquest of Makkah, Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah secretly wrote to the Quraysh warning them of the Prophet's intended march. Allah informed the Prophet, the letter was retrieved, and Hatib admitted what he had done; this verse was revealed forbidding the betrayal of trusts.
8:27.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:28.occasion: O you who believe! Betray not Allah and His Messenger, nor betray knowingly your Amanat (things entrusted to you)(27)And know that your possessions and your children are but a trial and that surely, with Allah is a mighty reward (28) Reason behind revealing This Ayah, and the prohibition of Betrayal The Two Sahihs mention the story of Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah. In the year of the victory of Makkah he wrote to the Quraysh alerting them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to march towards them. Allah informed His Messenger ﷺ of this, and he sent a Companion to retrieve the letter that Hatib sent, and then he summoned him.

8:30.occasion: The chiefs of Quraysh gathered at Dar An-Nadwah and plotted against the Prophet, debating whether to imprison him, expel him, or have young men from every clan strike him down together. Jibril warned the Prophet not to sleep in his bed that night and he migrated; this verse was later revealed reminding him of their plot.
8:30.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:36.occasion: After their defeat at Badr, leading men of Quraysh who had lost relatives went to Abu Sufyan and those whose wealth was in the caravan, urging them to spend that wealth to finance fighting against the Prophet. This verse was revealed about their spending to hinder others from the path of Allah.
8:36.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:37.occasion: Verily, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to hinder (men) from the path of Allah, and so will they continue to spend it; but in the end it will become an anguish for them. Then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered unto Hell (36)In order that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, and put the wicked one over another, heap them together and cast them into Hell.

8:41.occasion: And know that whatever of war booty that you may gain, verily, one-fifth of it is assigned to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives (of the Messenger), the orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and in that which We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the Day when the two forces met; and Allah is able to do all things (41) Ruling on the Spoils of War (Ghanimah and Fai') Allah explains the spoils of war in detail, as He has specifically allowed it for this honorable Ummah over all others.

__setting_9.label: 10 AH · 631 CE · Madinah
__setting_9.context: Revealed in Madinah during the mature Medinan period (7–10 AH / 628–632 CE), as the Muslim state grew in strength. The conquest of Makkah (8 AH), the campaigns to the north, and the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH) all occurred in this period. The Quran was approaching completion.

9:19.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that this passage was revealed concerning Al-Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib. When he was taken captive at the battle of Badr and was reproached for his disbelief, he boasted that the idolaters used to maintain Al-Masjid Al-Haram, provide water for the pilgrims, and free the indebted. Allah then revealed that such deeds, done in a state of Shirk, are not equal to faith and Jihad.

9:20.occasion: Do you consider the providing of drinking water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of Al-Masjid Al-Haram as equal to the worth of those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and strive hard and fight in the cause of Allah They are not equal before Allah. 9:49.occasion: This was revealed about Al-Jadd bin Qays, a chief of Banu Salimah. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) invited him to march to Tabuk against the Romans, he asked to be excused, claiming that he feared he could not restrain himself if he saw the Roman women, and asking not to be put to trial. Allah declared that he had already fallen into trial.
9:49.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:65.occasion: Abdullah bin Umar reported that during the Tabuk expedition a man in a gathering mocked the Qur'an reciters, calling them the greediest, most lying, and most cowardly. A Muslim rebuked him as a hypocrite and reported him to the Prophet (peace be upon him). When confronted, the man pleaded that he was only talking idly and jesting, and this passage was revealed.
9:65.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:66.occasion: If you ask them (about this), they declare: "We were only talking idly and joking." Say: "Was it at Allah, and His Ayat and His Messenger that you were mocking (65)Make no excuse; you disbelieved after you had believed. If We pardon some of you, We will punish others among you because they were criminals (66) The Hypocrites rely on False, Misguided Excuses Abdullah bin 'Umar said, "During the battle of Tabuk, a man was sitting in a gathering and said, 'I have never seen like these reciters of ours! They have the hungriest stomachs, the most lying tongues and are the most cowardice in battle.' A man in the Masjid said, 'You lie.

9:73.occasion: O Prophet! Strive hard against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh against them, their abode is Hell, – and worst indeed is that destination (73)They swear by Allah that they said nothing (bad), but really they said the word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after accepting Islam, and they resolved that (plot) which they were unable to carry out, and they could not find any cause to do so except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them of His bounty. If then they repent, it will be better for them, but if they turn away; Allah will punish them with a painful torment in this worldly life and in the Hereafter.

9:74.occasion: This was revealed about Al-Julas bin Suwayd, one of the hypocrites who lagged behind. He said that if Muhammad (peace be upon him) was telling the truth, they were worse than donkeys. His stepson Umayr bin Sa'd reported this to the Prophet, and Al-Julas swore by Allah that he had said nothing of the sort, so this verse was sent down. It is also said the verse refers to the hypocrites who plotted to throw the Prophet from the mountain pass at Tabuk.
9:74.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:79.occasion: This was revealed when the Prophet (peace be upon him) called the people to give charity. Abdur-Rahman bin Awf gave a large amount and the hypocrites accused him of showing off, while Abu Aqil brought only a small measure (a Sa') of dates and they mocked him, saying Allah had no need of it. Allah rebuked those who defamed both the generous and the poor giver.
9:79.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:84.occasion: Ibn Umar reported that when Abdullah bin Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, died, his son asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) for his shirt as a shroud and asked him to pray the funeral prayer over him. The Prophet did so despite Umar's objection. Afterwards this verse was revealed forbidding the Prophet from ever praying over a hypocrite who dies or standing at his grave.
9:84.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:102.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that this was revealed about Abu Lubabah and a group with him who stayed behind from the battle of Tabuk. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) returned, they tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque and refused to be untied by anyone but him. When the verse was revealed, the Prophet untied them and pardoned them.
9:102.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:106.occasion: And others are made to await for Allah's Decree, whether He will punish them or will forgive them. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise (106) Delaying the Decision about the Three Companions Who stayed away from the Battle of Tabuk Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak and several others said that those mentioned in the Ayah are the three who were made to wait to know if their repentance was accepted; Mararah bin Ar-Rabi', Ka'b bin Malik and Hilal bin Umayyah. Some Companions stayed behind from the battle of Tabuk due to laziness, preferring comfort, ease, ripe fruits and shade. They did not lag behind because of hypocrisy or doubts.

9:113.occasion: Al-Musayyib reported that when Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, was dying, the Prophet (peace be upon him) urged him to say 'La ilaha illa-llah,' but Abu Talib died upon the religion of Abdul-Muttalib. The Prophet said he would keep seeking forgiveness for him unless forbidden, and this verse was revealed prohibiting seeking forgiveness for the idolaters even if they are kin.
9:113.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:114.occasion: It is not (proper) for the Prophet and those who believe to ask Allah's forgiveness for the Mushrikin, even though they be of kin, after it has become clear to them that they are the dwellers of the Fire (because they died in a state of disbelief)(113)And Ibrahim's invoking (of Allah) for his father's forgiveness was only because of a promise he [Ibrahim] had made to him (his father). But when it became clear to him [Ibrahim] that he (his father) is an enemy of Allah, he dissociated himself from him.

9:117.occasion: Allah has forgiven the Prophet, the Muhajirin and the Ansar who followed him in the time of distress (Tabuk expedition), after the hearts of a party of them had nearly deviated (from the right path), but He accepted their repentance. Certainly, He is unto them full of kindness, Most Merciful (117) Battle of Tabuk Mujahid and several others said, "This Ayah was revealed concerning the battle of Tabuk. They left for that battle during a period of distress.

9:122.occasion: And it is not (proper) for the believers to go out (to fight - Jihad) all together. Of every troop of them, a party only should go forth, that they may get instructions in religion, and that they may warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware (of evil)(122) Allah the Exalted here explains His order to Muslims to march forth with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the battle of Tabuk.

__setting_10.label: Mid Makkah · ~617 CE
__setting_10.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

10:3.occasion: "Surely, your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days and then rose over (Istawa) the Throne, arranging the affair [of all things]. No intercessor (can plead with Him) except after He permits. That is Allah, your Lord; so worship Him (alone). Then, will you not remember (3) Allah is the Creator Who arranges the Affairs of the Universe Allah tells us that He is the Lord of the entire existence. He tells us that He created the heavens and the earth in six days.

10:17.occasion: So who does more wrong than he who forges a lie against Allah or denies His Āyāt? Surely, the criminals will never be successful (17) Allah says that no one is more wrong, unjust and arrogant than he who invented a lie against Allah, forged claims about Allah,or claimed that Allah has sent a message to him but his claim was not true. No one is more of a criminal or has committed greater wrong than such a person. Liars cannot be confused with Prophets. Anyone who claims such a thing, whether lying or telling the truth, will necessarily be supported by Allah with proofs and signs of his falsehood or truthfulness.

10:20.occasion: And they say: "How is it that not a sign is sent down on him from his Lord?" Say: "The Unseen belongs only to Allah, so wait you, verily, I am with you among those who wait. (20) The Idolators requested a Miracle These stubborn, lying disbelievers said, "Why would not a sign be revealed to Muhammad from his Lord." They meant a sign such as given to Salih. Allah sent the she-camel to Thamud. They wanted Allah to change the mount of As-Safa into gold or remove the mountains of Makkah and replace them with gardens and rivers. Allah is capable of doing all of that, but He is All-Wise in His actions and statements.

11:114.occasion: A man kissed a woman who was not lawful to him and then came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and told him what he had done. When the man asked if it was only for him, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said it was for all of his followers.

__setting_17.label: Mid Makkah · ~616 CE
__setting_17.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

17:1.occasion: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) told the people of Makkah about his Night Journey to Jerusalem and back in a single night, the Quraysh rejected it and some who had embraced Islam abandoned the faith. When the doubters went to Abu Bakr, he affirmed that whatever the Prophet said was true, and from then on he was known as As-Siddiq.
17:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:2.occasion: And We gave Musa the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel (saying): "Take none other than Me as (your) Wakil. (2)"O offspring of those whom We carried (in the ship) with Nuh! Verily, he was a grateful servant. (3) Musa and how He was given the Tawrah When Allah mentions how He took His servant Muhammad ﷺ, on the Journey by Night, He follows it by mentioning Musa, His servant and Messenger who also spoke with Him. Allah often mentions Muhammad and Musa together, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon them both, and he mentions the Tawrah and the Qur'an together.

17:90.occasion: The leaders of the Quraysh gathered behind the Kabah and summoned the Prophet (peace be upon him), offering him wealth, leadership, or kingship to abandon his message, then demanding that he produce specific signs such as causing a spring to gush forth, growing gardens, making the sky fall in pieces, or ascending to heaven and bringing down a book they could read. These verses were revealed concerning their demands.
17:90.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:110.occasion: An idolator heard the Prophet (peace be upon him) saying in prostration, 'O Most Gracious (Ar-Rahman), O Most Merciful,' and claimed that he prays to two while saying he prays to One, so the verse was revealed that by whichever name Allah is invoked, to Him belong the best names. It was also revealed because when the Prophet recited aloud in prayer the idolators would insult the Quran, so he was told to recite neither too loudly nor too softly but to follow a way between.
17:110.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:111.occasion: Say: "Invoke Allah or invoke Ar-Rahman (the Most Gracious), by whatever name you invoke Him (it is the same), for to Him belong the Best Names. And offer your Salah (prayer) neither aloud nor in a low voice, but follow a way between (110)And say: "All the praises and thanks be to Allah, Who has not begotten a son, and Who has no partner in (His) dominion, nor is He low to have a supporter. And magnify Him with all magnificence.

__setting_18.label: Late Makkah · ~619 CE
__setting_18.context: Revealed during the final chapter of the Makkan struggle (~618–622 CE), as the Prophet prepared for migration (Hijra) to Madinah. The Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Mi'raj) occurred in this period, and small delegations from Madinah began accepting Islam at Aqabah.

18:1.occasion: The Quraysh sent An-Nadr bin Al-Harith and 'Uqbah bin Abi Mu'it to the Jewish rabbis in Madinah, who told them to test the Prophet by asking him about some young men of ancient times, about a man who traveled to the east and west of the earth, and about the Ruh (the spirit). When they questioned him, the Prophet said he would answer the next day but did not say 'If Allah wills,' so revelation was delayed for fifteen days. Then this Surah was revealed, telling him about the young men of the Cave and the traveler.
18:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

18:23.occasion: This relates to the same incident: when the Prophet was asked about the people of the Cave he replied 'I will tell you tomorrow' without saying 'If Allah wills,' and revelation was then withheld for fifteen days, after which he was taught the etiquette of always referring his future intentions to the will of Allah.
18:23.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

18:24.occasion: And never say of anything, "I shall do such and such thing tomorrow. (23)Except (with the saying), "If Allah wills!" And remember your Lord when you forget and say: "It may be that my Lord guides me to a nearer way of truth than this. (24) Saying "If Allah wills" when determining to do Something in the Future Here Allah, may He be glorified, shows His Messenger ﷺ the correct etiquette when determining to do something in the future; this should always be referred to the will of Allah, the Knower of the Unseen, Who knows what was and what is yet to be and what is not to be, and how it will be if it is to be.

18:27.occasion: And recite what has been revealed to you (O Muhammad) of your Lord's Book. None can change His Words, and none will you find as refuge other than Him (27)And keep yourself (O Muhammad) patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and afternoon, seeking His Face; and let not your eyes overlook them, desiring the pomp and glitter of the life of the world; and obey not him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his own lusts, and whose affair has been lost (28) The Command to recite the Qur'an and to patiently keep Company with the Believers Commanding His Messenger ﷺ to recite His Holy Book and convey it to…

18:28.occasion: The nobles of Quraysh asked the Prophet to sit with them alone and to send away his poor and weak Companions, such as Bilal, 'Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab and Ibn Mas'ud, so they would not be offended by their presence. Allah forbade him from driving them away and commanded him to remain patiently in the company of those who call upon their Lord.
18:28.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

18:32.occasion: Ibn Kathir states that the parable of the two men, one of whom owned two gardens, was revealed concerning Al-'As bin Wa'il.
18:32.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_19.label: Mid Makkah · ~616 CE
__setting_19.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

__setting_22.label: 6 AH · 627 CE · Madinah
__setting_22.context: Revealed in Madinah during the middle Medinan period (3–7 AH / 625–628 CE), as the Muslim community faced the Battles of Uhud and al-Khandaq (Trench), dealt with hypocrites within its ranks, and consolidated its social and legal institutions. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded near the end of this period.

22:3.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from As-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, that this verse was revealed concerning An-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and that Ibn Jurayj held the same view.
22:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

22:4.occasion: And among mankind is he who disputes about Allah, without knowledge, and follows every rebellious Shaytan (3)For him (the devil) it is decreed that whosoever follows him, he will mislead him, and will drive him to the torment of the Fire (4) Condemnation of the Followers of the Shaytan Allah condemns those who deny the Resurrection and who deny that Allah is able to restore life to the dead, those who turn away from that which Allah has revealed to His Prophets and, in their views – denial and disbelief – follow every rebellious Shaytan among men and Jinn.

22:19.occasion: Recorded in the Two Sahihs, Abu Dharr swore that this verse was revealed concerning the men who came forward for single combat at the Battle of Badr: Hamzah, 'Ali and 'Ubaydah on one side, and 'Utbah, Shaybah and Al-Walid on the other.
22:19.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_24.label: 6 AH · 627 CE · Madinah
__setting_24.context: Revealed in Madinah during the middle Medinan period (3–7 AH / 625–628 CE), as the Muslim community faced the Battles of Uhud and al-Khandaq (Trench), dealt with hypocrites within its ranks, and consolidated its social and legal institutions. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded near the end of this period.

24:11.occasion: These verses were revealed concerning Aishah, the mother of the believers, after the hypocrites led by Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul spread a false accusation against her (the event of Al-Ifk). She had been accidentally left behind by the army when she went back to look for a lost necklace, and Safwan bin al-Mu'attal brought her to Madinah on his camel. The slander circulated for about a month until Allah revealed her innocence.
24:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:12.occasion: Why then, did not the believers, men and women, when you heard it, think good of their own people and say: "This is an obvious lie? (12)Why did they not produce four witnesses against him? Since they have not produced witnesses! Then with Allah, they are the liars (13) Disciplining the Believers for Spreading the Slander Here Allah disciplines the believers with regard to the matter of 'A'ishah, because some of them spread this evil talk and the slander that had been mentioned.

24:13.occasion: Why then, did not the believers, men and women, when you heard it, think good of their own people and say: "This is an obvious lie? 24:22.occasion: This verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, who had sworn that he would never again spend on his poor relative Mistah bin Uthathah after Mistah took part in the slander against Aishah. When the verse was revealed, Abu Bakr resumed his support of Mistah, saying he loved that Allah should forgive him.
24:22.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:26.occasion: Bad statements are for bad people and bad people for bad statements. Good statements are for good people and good people for good statements: such are innocent of (every) bad statement which they say; for them is forgiveness, and honored provision (26) The Goodness of 'A'ishah Because She is Married to the Best of Mankind Ibn 'Abbas said, "Evil words are for evil men, and evil men are for evil words; good words are for good men and good men are for good words.

24:31.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Muqatil bin Hayyan that the reason for the revelation of this verse was that Asma' bint Murshidah, in her home among Banu Harithah, saw women coming in without proper covering so that their anklets, chests and forelocks were exposed, and she remarked how ugly this was; then Allah revealed the command for believing women to lower their gaze and cover themselves.
24:31.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:32.occasion: And marry those among you who are single (Al-Ayama) and the pious of your servants and maidservants. If they be poor, Allah will enrich them out of His bounty. And Allah is All-Sufficent, All-Knowing (32)And let those who find not the financial means for marriage keep themselves chaste, until Allah enriches them of His bounty. And such of your servants as seek a writing (of emancipation), give them such writing, if you find that there is good and honesty in them. And give them something (yourselves) out of the wealth of Allah which He has bestowed upon you.

24:33.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that the prohibition against forcing slave-girls into prostitution was revealed concerning Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who used to compel his slave-girls (such as Musaykah and Mu'adhah) to commit immorality so that he could take their earnings, even though they wished to remain chaste.
24:33.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:36.occasion: In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised, in them His Name is remembered. 24:37.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn Umar that this verse, describing men whom neither trade nor business diverts from the remembrance of Allah, was revealed concerning people who, when the call to prayer was given while they were in the marketplace, would close their shops and hasten to the mosque.
24:37.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:55.occasion: Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous good deeds, that He will certainly grant them succession in the land, as He granted it to those before them, and that He will grant them the authority to practise their religion which He has chosen for them. And He will surely give them in exchange a safe security after their fear if they worship Me and do not associate anything with Me.

24:61.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that this verse granting permission to eat in the houses of relatives and friends was revealed because the Muslims, after the revelation forbidding them to consume one another's property unjustly, felt it was unlawful to eat in each other's homes; some also felt embarrassed to eat together with the blind, lame and sick. Allah thus removed this difficulty.
24:61.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_25.label: Mid Makkah · ~615 CE
__setting_25.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

28:52.occasion: Sa'id bin Jubayr reported that these verses were revealed concerning a delegation of about seventy priests sent by An-Najashi (the Negus of Ethiopia). When they came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, he recited Surah Ya Sin to them; they wept and embraced Islam, and these verses about those who already believed before the Qur'an were revealed concerning them.

28:56.occasion: Recorded in the Two Sahihs as having been revealed concerning Abu Talib, the paternal uncle of the Prophet, peace be upon him, who protected and loved him out of kinship. As Abu Talib lay dying, the Prophet urged him to say La ilaha illallah, but Abu Jahl and 'Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah pressed him to remain on the religion of 'Abdul-Muttalib, and he died refusing to make the declaration.

33:4.occasion: Revealed concerning Zayd bin Harithah, the freed servant whom the Prophet had adopted before prophethood and who used to be called Zayd bin Muhammad. Allah ended this practice, declaring that adopted sons are not real sons and should be named after their own fathers.

33:5.occasion: Allah has not made for any man two hearts inside his body. But if you know not their father's, your brothers in faith and Mawalikum (your freed servants). And there is no sin on you concerning that in which you made a mistake, except in regard to what your hearts deliberately intend.

__setting_38.label: Mid Makkah · ~615 CE
__setting_38.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

38:4.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that when Abu Talib fell ill, leaders of the Quraysh, including Abu Jahl, came to him and complained that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was insulting their gods. The Prophet was summoned and asked them to accept a single statement, 'La ilaha illallah,' by which the Arabs and non-Arabs would submit to them. They stood up in agitation and said this was a curious thing, and this passage (verses 4 through 8) was then revealed.
38:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_39.label: Mid Makkah · ~618 CE
__setting_39.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

39:17.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports, on the authority of 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam from his father, that the verse about those who avoid worshipping false gods (At-Taghut) and turn to Allah was revealed concerning Zayd bin 'Amr bin Nufayl, Abu Dharr, and Salman Al-Farisi. He adds that the correct view is that it includes them and all others who shunned idols and turned to the worship of the Most Merciful.
39:17.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

39:23.occasion: Allah has sent down the Best Statement, a Book, its parts resembling each other, (and) oft-repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it. Then their skin and their heart soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah. He guides therewith whom He wills; and whomever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide (23) The Description of the Qur'an Here Allah praises His Book, the Noble Qur'an, which was revealed to His noble Messenger ﷺ.

44:10.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn Mas'ud that when the Quraysh refused Islam and grew stubborn, the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed against them that they would suffer years of drought and famine like the years of Yusuf. They were struck by such severe hunger that they ate bones and dead meat, and out of exhaustion a man would look at the sky and see only a smoky haze. This was connected to the verse about the day the sky brings forth a visible smoke.

46:15.occasion: This verse enjoining kindness to parents was revealed concerning Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas (RA), whose mother swore she would neither eat nor drink until he renounced his faith, abstaining so stubbornly that they had to force her mouth open with a stick.
46:15.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

46:16.occasion: And We have enjoined on man to be dutiful and kind to his parents. His mother bears him with hardship. And she delivers him with hardship. And (the period of) his gestation and the weaning of him is thirty months, till when he attains full strength and reaches forty years, he says: "My Lord! Grant me the power and ability that I may be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and that I may do righteous good deeds, such as please You, and make my offspring good. Truly, I have turned to You in repentance, and truly, I am one of the Muslims.

46:17.occasion: But he who says to his parents: "Uff to you! Do you promise me that I will be raised up when generations before me have passed?" While they invoke Allah for help: "Woe to you! Believe! Verily, the promise of Allah is true." But he says: "This is nothing but the legends of the ancient. (17)They are those against whom the Word (of torment) has justified among the previous generations of Jinn and mankind that have passed away. Verily, they are ever the losers (18)And for all, there will be degrees according to that which they did, so that He might fully recompense for their deeds.

__setting_47.label: 4 AH · 625 CE · Madinah
__setting_47.context: Revealed in Madinah during the middle Medinan period (3–7 AH / 625–628 CE), as the Muslim community faced the Battles of Uhud and al-Khandaq (Trench), dealt with hypocrites within its ranks, and consolidated its social and legal institutions. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded near the end of this period.

47:4.occasion: Ibn Kathir notes that this verse, with its ruling on captives and freeing them by grace or ransom, appears to have been revealed after the battle of Badr, when Allah reproached the believers for sparing many of the enemy and holding too many captives in order to take ransom from them.
47:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

47:5.occasion: So, when you meet those who disbelieve (in battle), smite (their) necks until you have fully defeated them, then tighten their bonds. Thereafter (is the time) either for generosity or ransom, until the war lays down its burden. Thus, and had Allah so willed, He could have taken vengeance against them;–but (He lets you struggle) so as to test with one another.

__setting_48.label: 9 AH · 630 CE · Madinah
__setting_48.context: Revealed in Madinah during the mature Medinan period (7–10 AH / 628–632 CE), as the Muslim state grew in strength. The conquest of Makkah (8 AH), the campaigns to the north, and the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH) all occurred in this period. The Quran was approaching completion.

48:1.occasion: This Surah was revealed after the Messenger of Allah returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhul-Qa'dah of the sixth year of Hijrah, after the idolators had prevented him from reaching the Sacred House for 'Umrah and a peace treaty was concluded. Anas reported that the verse was revealed on the Prophet's return from Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the Prophet recited it to the Companions as glad tidings.
48:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_49.label: 7 AH · 628 CE · Madinah
__setting_49.context: Revealed in Madinah during the middle Medinan period (3–7 AH / 625–628 CE), as the Muslim community faced the Battles of Uhud and al-Khandaq (Trench), dealt with hypocrites within its ranks, and consolidated its social and legal institutions. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded near the end of this period.

49:4.occasion: It was reported, according to more than one source, that this verse was revealed concerning Al-Aqra bin Habis At-Tamimi, who came and called out to the Prophet (peace be upon him) from behind his dwellings, repeatedly saying, 'O Muhammad! O Muhammad!'
49:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:9.occasion: Said bin Jubayr related that the tribes of Aws and Khazraj once came to blows, striking one another with date-palm branches and sandals, and Allah revealed this verse commanding that peace be made between them. It was also reported that a quarrel broke out when a man of the Ansar confined his wife and her family came to take her, leading the two groups to fight, after which the Prophet (peace be upon him) sent someone to reconcile them.
49:9.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:10.occasion: And if two parties among the believers fall to fighting, then make peace between them both. But if one of them outrages against the other, then fight you (all) against the one that which outrages till it complies with the command of Allah. Then if it complies, then make reconciliation between them justly, and be equitable. Verily, Allah loves those who are the equitable (9)The believers are but a brotherhood.

49:11.occasion: Abu Jabirah bin Ad-Dahhak said this verse was revealed concerning Banu Salamah. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) came to Madinah, every man among them had two or three nicknames, and when he called a man by one of them people would say he disliked that name, so the prohibition against insulting one another by nicknames was revealed.
49:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_50.label: Mid Makkah · ~614 CE
__setting_50.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

__setting_51.label: Late Makkah · ~619 CE
__setting_51.context: Revealed during the final chapter of the Makkan struggle (~618–622 CE), as the Prophet prepared for migration (Hijra) to Madinah. The Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Mi'raj) occurred in this period, and small delegations from Madinah began accepting Islam at Aqabah.

57:26.occasion: And indeed, We sent Nuh and Ibrahim, and placed in their offspring prophethood and Scripture. And among them there are some who are guided; but many of them are rebellious (26)Then, We sent after them Our Messengers, and We sent 'Isa the son of Maryam, and gave him the Injil. 57:27.occasion: Ibn Abbas related that after 'Isa, kings altered the Tawrah and Injil while some believers still recited the originals. Persecuted and threatened with death unless they abandoned the true scriptures, these believers withdrew from society, some building towers, some wandering the land, and some constructing hermitages in deserts where they could worship in seclusion. Ibn Kathir reports that the portion of this verse about the monasticism people invented for themselves was revealed concerning them.

58:2.occasion: When Khawlah bint Tha'labah complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him) about the Zihar her husband Aws bin As-Samit had pronounced and the hardship she suffered, Allah revealed the ruling on Zihar and its expiation. 59:2.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that this surah was revealed concerning the Jewish tribe of Bani An-Nadir. After they betrayed their treaty with the Prophet and plotted to kill him by dropping a stone on him while he sat by a wall of their houses, he laid siege to their forts and they were exiled from Al-Madinah, leaving their homes and wealth behind.
59:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

59:5.occasion: When the Prophet ordered the date trees of Bani An-Nadir to be cut down and burned during the siege, the Jews objected that he had forbidden mischief in the land, and some of the Muslims hesitated, asking whether they would be rewarded for what they cut or blamed for what they left standing. This verse was then revealed declaring that whatever was felled or left was by Allah's leave.
59:5.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

60:10.occasion: After the treaty of Al-Hudaybiyyah, which stipulated that anyone coming over to the Muslims be returned, believing women began emigrating to Madinah. When Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah emigrated and her brothers came demanding her return, Allah revealed this verse exempting the women from the treaty, commanding that their faith be tested and that they not be sent back to the disbelievers.
60:10.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

60:11.occasion: O you who believe! When believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them; Allah knows best as to their faith, then if you ascertain that they are true believers, send them not back to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for the disbelievers nor are the disbelievers lawful for them. But give them (disbelievers) that which they have spent (on their dowery). And there will be no sin on you to marry them if you have paid their due to them. Likewise do not keep the disbelieving women, and ask for that which you have spent (on their dowery) and let them (the disbelievers) ask for that which they have spent.

61:2.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Muqatil bin Hayyan that the believers had said that if they only knew the dearest deeds to Allah they would perform them; they were then tested on the day of Uhud, where they retreated and fled, leaving the Prophet (peace be upon him) behind, and it was concerning their case that this verse was revealed. He also cites Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak that it was sent down to rebuke people who falsely claimed they had fought, killed, and stabbed in battle when they had done none of it.
61:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

74:24.occasion: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah entered the house of Abu Bakr and asked about the Qur'an, then told the Quraysh that it was not poetry, magic, or madness but the Word of Allah. The Quraysh feared his conversion would lead all of them to convert, so Abu Jahl went to him and provoked him by claiming his people said he only visited Abu Bakr to get his food. Al-Walid then declared the Qur'an to be merely 'inherited magic of old,' and Allah revealed the passage beginning 'Leave Me alone with whom I created lonely' through 'It spares not, nor does it leave.'
74:24.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_75.label: Mid Makkah · ~614 CE
__setting_75.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

75:16.occasion: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to move his tongue and lips hurriedly, repeating the revelation along with the angel out of fear that he would forget it. Allah then revealed these verses instructing him not to hasten with the Qur'an, but to listen, for Allah Himself would gather it in his heart and enable him to recite and understand it.
75:16.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_76.label: 5 AH · 626 CE · Madinah
__setting_76.context: Revealed in Madinah during the middle Medinan period (3–7 AH / 625–628 CE), as the Muslim community faced the Battles of Uhud and al-Khandaq (Trench), dealt with hypocrites within its ranks, and consolidated its social and legal institutions. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded near the end of this period.

__setting_77.label: Mid Makkah · ~614 CE
__setting_77.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

77:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn Mas'ud that this Surah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah while they were with him in a cave at Mina. Ibn Mas'ud was learning it directly from the Prophet's mouth when a snake suddenly appeared and was killed.
77:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_78.label: Late Makkah · ~621 CE
__setting_78.context: Revealed during the final chapter of the Makkan struggle (~618–622 CE), as the Prophet prepared for migration (Hijra) to Madinah. The Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Mi'raj) occurred in this period, and small delegations from Madinah began accepting Islam at Aqabah.
