__setting_82.label: Late Makkah · ~621 CE
__setting_82.context: Revealed during the final chapter of the Makkan struggle (~618–622 CE), as the Prophet prepared for migration (Hijra) to Madinah. The Night Journey and Ascension (Isra and Mi'raj) occurred in this period, and small delegations from Madinah began accepting Islam at Aqabah.

82:6.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Al-Baghawi that Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said this verse, 'What has made you careless about your Lord, the Most Generous?', was revealed concerning Al-Aswad bin Shariq, who struck the Prophet and was not punished in retaliation, whereupon Allah revealed it.
82:6.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_87.label: Early Makkah · ~610 CE
__setting_87.context: Revealed in the earliest years of the Prophetic mission in Makkah (~610–612 CE), when the community of believers was small and largely from among the weak and marginalized. The Quraysh had begun to mock and ostracize the Muslims, but open persecution had not yet begun.

87:1.occasion: The Virtues of Surat Al-A'la This Surah was revealed in Makkah before the migration to Al-Madinah. The proof of this is what Al-Bukhari recorded from Al-Bara' bin 'Azib, that he said, "The first people to come to us (in Al-Madinah) from the Companions of the Prophet were ﷺ Mus'ab bin 'Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum, who taught us the Qur'an; then 'Ammar, Bilal and Sa'd came. Then 'Umar bin Al-Khattab came with a group of twenty people, after which the Prophet ﷺ came. I have not seen the people of Al-Madinah happier with anything more than their happiness with his coming (to Al-Madinah).

92:5.occasion: Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Amir bin 'Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr that Abu Bakr used to free weak servants, the elderly, and women in Makkah when they accepted Islam. When his father urged him instead to free strong men who could defend him, Abu Bakr replied that he sought only what is with Allah. Some of his family said this Ayah was revealed concerning him.
92:5.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

92:17.occasion: Many of the scholars of Tafsir mentioned that these Ayat were revealed about Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, and some even reported a consensus on this. He was foremost in giving his wealth in obedience to Allah and in aiding the Messenger of Allah, seeking only the Face of his Lord and expecting no favor in return.
92:17.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_109.context: Revealed in the earliest years of the Prophetic mission in Makkah (~610–612 CE), when the community of believers was small and largely from among the weak and marginalized. The Quraysh had begun to mock and ostracize the Muslims, but open persecution had not yet begun.

__setting_110.label: 10 AH · 631 CE · Madinah
__setting_110.context: Revealed in Madinah during the mature Medinan period (7–10 AH / 628–632 CE), as the Muslim state grew in strength. The conquest of Makkah (8 AH), the campaigns to the north, and the Farewell Pilgrimage (10 AH) all occurred in this period. The Quran was approaching completion.

__setting_111.label: Early Makkah · ~610 CE
__setting_111.context: Revealed in the earliest years of the Prophetic mission in Makkah (~610–612 CE), when the community of believers was small and largely from among the weak and marginalized. The Quraysh had begun to mock and ostracize the Muslims, but open persecution had not yet begun.

__setting_112.label: Mid Makkah · ~612 CE
__setting_112.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

112:1.occasion: Imam Ahmad recorded from Ubayy bin Ka'b that the idolators said to the Prophet, 'O Muhammad! Tell us the lineage of your Lord.' So Allah revealed this Surah.
112:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

__setting_113.label: Early Makkah · ~612 CE
__setting_113.context: Revealed in the earliest years of the Prophetic mission in Makkah (~610–612 CE), when the community of believers was small and largely from among the weak and marginalized. The Quraysh had begun to mock and ostracize the Muslims, but open persecution had not yet begun.

__setting_114.label: Mid Makkah · ~612 CE
__setting_114.context: Revealed during the middle Makkan period (~613–617 CE), as the message spread publicly and persecution intensified. Weaker companions were tortured, the economic boycott of Banu Hashim was imposed, and the Prophet's wife Khadijah and uncle Abu Talib passed away in the Year of Grief.

36:8.occasion: Ikrimah reported that Abu Jahl said, 'If I see Muhammad, I will do such and such,' threatening the Prophet. Then Allah revealed the verses, 'Verily, We have put on their necks iron collars... so that they cannot see.' Afterwards, when people pointed out the Prophet to him, Abu Jahl would say, 'Where is he?' and was unable to see him.
36:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

105:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir explains this surah recounts one of Allah's favors to the Quraysh: He saved them from the People of the Elephant, who had come to tear down the Ka'bah and wipe out all trace of it. Abrahah Al-Ashram, the Abyssinian governor of Yemen, had built a great church in San'a' and sought to divert the Arabs' pilgrimage to it; when a man of the Quraysh defiled it, Abrahah swore to destroy the Ka'bah and marched on Makkah with a huge army led by a great elephant named Mahmud. According to the most popular opinion, the Messenger of Allah was born during that same year, so the event was a sign preparing the way for his coming.
105:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

105:5.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates that when Abrahah's army turned the elephant toward Makkah it knelt and refused to advance, so Allah sent against them birds from the sea, each carrying three stones the size of chickpeas and lentils, which struck the men and destroyed them; Abrahah himself was broken down limb by limb and died after his heart fell from his chest upon reaching San'a'. Allah thus annihilated them and routed their plot, and afterward the Prophet would recount this deliverance to the Quraysh as a blessing Allah had bestowed upon them.
105:5.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

111:1.occasion: Al-Bukhari recorded from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (peace be upon him) went out to the valley of Al-Batha, ascended the mountain, and cried out to gather the Quraysh. He asked whether they would believe him if he warned them of an approaching enemy, and when they affirmed, he said, 'Verily, I am a warner to you all before the coming of a severe torment.' Abu Lahab then said, 'Have you gathered us for this? May you perish!' so Allah revealed this Surah.
111:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

80:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that while the Messenger of Allah was earnestly speaking with one of the great leaders of the Quraysh, hoping he would accept Islam, the blind man Ibn Umm Maktum, an early Muslim, came urgently asking to be taught. The Prophet frowned and turned away from him to continue with the noble man, and these verses were revealed reproving that and commanding that warning be given equally to noble and weak alike. Ibn Kathir also cites 'A'ishah that the passage was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum the blind man, who came saying 'Guide me' while a great idolater leader was present.
80:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

83:1.occasion: An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah recorded from Ibn 'Abbas that when the Prophet came to Al-Madinah, its people were the worst of people in giving measure, cheating in it. So Allah revealed 'Woe to Al-Mutaffifin.' After this, they began to give full and good measure.
83:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

85:4.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn Ishaq's Sirah that these verses were revealed concerning the People of the Ditch, identified as Dhu Nuwas (Yusuf, son of Tuban As'ad Abi Karib) and his army, who called the believing Christians of Najran to abandon their faith for Judaism. When they refused, he had ditches dug and burned and killed about twenty thousand of them, and it was about this that Allah revealed verses 85:4-9.
85:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:13.occasion: After Allah granted the Muslims victory at Badr and the Prophet (peace be upon him) returned to Al-Madinah, he gathered the Jews in the marketplace of Bani Qaynuqa' and warned them. This passage was addressed to them, pointing to the two armies that met at Badr as a sign that Allah would make His religion prevail.
3:13.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:61.occasion: A delegation of about sixty Christians from Najran came to Al-Madinah and argued that 'Isa was divine and the son of God. The opening verses of the surah, up to this point, were revealed to refute their claims, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) was commanded to call them to the Mubahalah (mutual invocation of Allah's curse upon the liars) when they persisted.
3:61.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:65.occasion: The Christians of Najran and the Jewish rabbis disputed before the Prophet (peace be upon him), the Jews claiming that Ibrahim was a Jew and the Christians claiming he was a Christian. This verse was revealed in response, pointing out that the Tawrah and Injil were sent down only after his time.
3:65.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:86.occasion: A man from the Ansar embraced Islam, then reverted and joined the polytheists. He later regretted this and sent his people to ask the Prophet (peace be upon him) whether he could repent. These verses, ending with the mention of Allah's forgiveness, were revealed, and he returned to Islam.
3:86.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:92.occasion: When this verse was revealed, Abu Talhah, who owned the Bayruha' garden that he loved most among his property and which faced the Prophet's Masjid, gave it away in charity for Allah's sake. The Prophet (peace be upon him) advised him to distribute it among his close relatives.
3:92.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:144.occasion: During the battle of Uhud a rumor spread that the Prophet (peace be upon him) had been killed, which weakened the resolve of some Muslims who stopped fighting. This verse was revealed reminding them that Muhammad is only a Messenger and that the death or killing of the Messenger must not turn them back from their religion.
3:144.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:181.occasion: When the verse calling for a goodly loan to Allah (2:245) was revealed, the Jews said, 'Has Allah become poor that He asks His servants for a loan?' This verse was revealed in response to their statement that Allah is poor and they are rich.
3:181.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:186.occasion: Before the battle of Badr, the Prophet (peace be upon him) passed a gathering that included 'Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who spoke offensively, and the Muslims, idolaters and Jews nearly came to blows. Allah commanded the believers to be patient and forbearing in the face of the abuse they would hear from the People of the Scripture and the idolaters.
3:186.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:195.occasion: Umm Salamah said, 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah does not mention women in connection with the Hijrah.' Then this verse was revealed, affirming that Allah will not let the work of any worker among them be lost, whether male or female.
3:195.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:7.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Jabir that Umm Kujjah came to the Messenger of Allah saying she had two daughters whose father had died and who owned nothing, after which this verse on inheritance shares for men and women was revealed.
4:7.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:11.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Jabir that the wife of Sa'd bin Ar-Rabi' came to the Prophet about her two daughters by Sa'd, who was martyred at Uhud, complaining that their uncle had taken all their inheritance. The verse of inheritance was then revealed, and the Prophet ordered two-thirds for the daughters, an eighth for their mother, and the rest for the uncle.
4:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:32.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates that Umm Salamah said to the Messenger of Allah that men go to battle while women do not and that women receive only half the inheritance of men, after which this verse was revealed telling them not to wish for what Allah favored some over others.
4:32.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:95.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites al-Bukhari that when the verse distinguishing those who sit at home from those who strive was being dictated, Ibn Umm Maktum mentioned that he was blind, whereupon the exception 'except those who are disabled' was revealed.
4:95.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:102.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Abu 'Ayyash az-Zuraqi that at 'Usfan the idolaters under Khalid bin al-Walid stood between the Muslims and the Qiblah and plotted to attack them during the 'Asr prayer. Jibril came down with the verses of the Fear prayer between Zuhr and 'Asr, and the Prophet led them accordingly.
4:102.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:176.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Jabir bin 'Abdullah that the Prophet visited him during a severe illness when he had fallen unconscious, and Jabir asked what to do about his inheritance since he would leave only collateral heirs (Kalalah). This concluding verse of the Surah, giving the ruling on Kalalah, was then revealed.
4:176.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:6.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites the report of 'A'ishah that on the return to Al-Madinah her necklace was lost at Al-Bayda', and the people were detained searching for it while there was no water. The Messenger of Allah slept there, and at dawn this verse on Wudu and Tayammum was revealed, so the people performed Tayammum.
5:6.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:108.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that the disbelievers said to the Prophet, 'You will stop insulting our gods, or we will insult your Lord.' So Allah forbade the believers from insulting the idols of the idolaters, lest they retaliate by insulting Allah out of ignorance. Qatadah related the same, that Muslims used to insult the idols and the disbelievers responded by insulting Allah.
6:108.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:121.occasion: As-Suddi reported that some idolaters challenged the Muslims, saying, 'You claim to seek Allah's pleasure, yet you do not eat what Allah causes to die, but you eat what you slaughter?' Thus Allah warned that if the believers obeyed them and ate carrion, they would indeed become idolaters.
6:121.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

7:28.occasion: The idolaters used to perform Tawaf around the Ka'bah while naked, claiming they would not circle it in clothes they had sinned in, and they alleged that Allah had commanded them to do so. This verse was revealed refuting their claim that such an indecency was commanded by Allah.
7:28.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:1.occasion: At Badr the Muslims disputed over the war spoils: those who had collected them, those who had pursued the enemy, and those who had guarded the Prophet each claimed a greater right. The verse was revealed taking the Anfal away from their dispute and assigning them to Allah and the Messenger, who then divided them equally among the Muslims.
8:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:19.occasion: At Badr Abu Jahl prayed, asking Allah to destroy whichever of the two armies had severed the ties of kinship and brought what was not recognized. This verse was revealed in response, telling the disbelievers that the judgement they had sought had now come to them.
8:19.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:32.occasion: Abu Jahl said: O Allah, if this Qur'an is indeed the truth from You, then rain down stones on us from the sky or bring us a painful torment. This verse, and the following verse about Allah not punishing them while the Prophet was among them, were revealed in response.
8:32.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:47.occasion: When the Quraysh set out toward Badr, Abu Jahl refused to turn back even after the caravan was safe, vowing to reach the wells of Badr to slaughter camels, drink, and have singing-girls perform so the Arabs would always speak of them. They marched out boastfully and to be seen of men, and this verse was revealed about them.
8:47.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:67.occasion: After Badr the Prophet consulted the Companions about the captives. Umar urged that they be executed, while Abu Bakr advised pardoning them in return for ransom; the Prophet accepted ransom. These verses were then revealed concerning the taking of captives and the ransom that was taken.
8:67.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:70.occasion: Al-Abbas, the Prophet's uncle, was captured at Badr and ransomed himself and his nephews, saying he had been left poor. This verse was revealed promising the captives that if Allah knew any good in their hearts He would give them better than what had been taken; Al-Abbas later said Allah replaced his loss many times over.
8:70.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:107.occasion: These verses were revealed about Masjid Ad-Dirar, which a group of hypocrites built next to Masjid Quba at the instigation of Abu Amir Ar-Rahib, who had fled to the Romans to seek their aid against the Prophet (peace be upon him). They intended it to harm the believers, spread disbelief, divide them, and serve as an outpost for Abu Amir, then invited the Prophet to pray in it. Allah forbade him, and on his return from Tabuk he ordered it demolished.
9:107.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:118.occasion: Ka'b bin Malik reported that this was revealed about himself and his two companions, Murarah bin Ar-Rabi' and Hilal bin Umayyah, who stayed behind from the Tabuk expedition without an excuse. Unlike the hypocrites, they told the Prophet (peace be upon him) the truth. He deferred their case and ordered the Muslims to shun them for fifty nights, until the earth was straitened for them, after which Allah revealed the acceptance of their repentance.
9:118.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

10:2.occasion: Ad-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas that when Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a Messenger, most of the Arabs denied him and his message, saying that Allah is greater than to send a human Messenger like Muhammad. So Allah revealed this verse rebuking their astonishment that revelation was sent to a man from among themselves.
10:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

12:3.occasion: Ibn Jarir At-Tabari recorded from Abdullah bin Abbas that the people said to the Messenger of Allah, 'Why do you not narrate stories to us?' In response this Ayah was revealed: 'We relate unto you the best of stories.'
12:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

13:8.occasion: These verses (13:8-11) were revealed concerning Arbad bin Qays and 'Amir bin At-Tufayl, who came to the Prophet in Al-Madinah plotting to kill him. 'Amir distracted the Prophet so Arbad could strike him with his sword, but Arbad's hand froze on the hilt and he could not draw it. As they departed, Allah struck Arbad dead with a thunderbolt of lightning, while 'Amir died of a sudden ulcer.
13:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

16:90.occasion: Reported from Ibn Abbas: while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was sitting with Uthman bin Maz'un, a messenger from Allah (the angel) came to him and conveyed this verse, 'Verily, Allah orders justice and kindness.' When Uthman heard it, faith became firmly established in his heart and he began to love the Prophet (peace be upon him).
16:90.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:45.occasion: When the surah condemning Abu Lahab was revealed, his wife Umm Jamil came seeking the Prophet (peace be upon him) with a stone in her hand to harm him while he sat with Abu Bakr. The Prophet recited Quran and Allah veiled him from her sight, so she could not see him though Abu Bakr was beside him.
17:45.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:59.occasion: The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) to turn the hill of As-Safa into gold and to remove the mountains so they could farm the land. He was offered the choice of granting their demand, after which they would be destroyed if they still disbelieved, or of giving them more time; he chose to give them respite, and this verse was revealed.
17:59.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:80.occasion: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was in Makkah and was then commanded to emigrate, so Allah revealed this verse asking that his entry and exit be made good and that he be granted a helping authority.
17:80.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

19:77.occasion: Khabbab bin Al-Aratt, a blacksmith, came to collect a debt from Al-'As bin Wa'il. Al-'As refused to pay unless Khabbab disbelieved in Muhammad, and mockingly claimed that when he was resurrected he would be given wealth and children and would repay him then. These verses were revealed in response.
19:77.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

20:2.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ad-Dahhak that when Allah revealed the Qur'an to His Messenger, he and his Companions held fast to it, so the idolaters of the Quraysh said, 'This Qur'an was only revealed to Muhammad to cause him distress.' In response Allah revealed Ta Ha, declaring that He did not send down the Qur'an to cause the Prophet distress, but only as a reminder to those who fear Allah.
20:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

22:11.occasion: Al-Bukhari recorded from Ibn 'Abbas that this was revealed about people who would come to Al-Madinah to declare their Islam: if their wives bore sons and their mares foaled they would say it was a good religion, but if not, they would say it was a bad religion and turn away.
22:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

23:76.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn 'Abbas that Abu Sufyan came to the Messenger of Allah and, appealing to him by Allah and by the ties of kinship between them, complained that the Quraysh had been reduced to eating camel hair and blood during the famine. Allah then revealed this verse, 'And indeed We seized them with punishment, but they humbled not themselves to their Lord.'
23:76.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:6.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that the verses of Li'an (mutual cursing) were revealed concerning Hilal bin Umayyah, who came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) accusing his wife of adultery with Sharik bin Sahma' but could not produce four witnesses. When he insisted he was truthful and feared the punishment for slander, Allah revealed the procedure of Li'an as a way out for him.
24:6.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:23.occasion: Ibn Kathir states that this warning against those who accuse chaste, believing women was revealed primarily concerning Aishah bint Abi Bakr, the mother of the believers, in the aftermath of the slander made against her.
24:23.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

26:214.occasion: When the verse 'And warn your tribe of near kindred' was revealed, the Prophet climbed As-Safa and called the clans of Quraysh together, asking whether they would believe him if he warned of a cavalry about to attack from behind the mountain; when they affirmed they would, he warned them of a severe punishment close at hand. Abu Lahab responded by cursing him and asking if this was all he had gathered them for, whereupon Surah 111 was revealed.
26:214.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

30:1.occasion: These verses were revealed when the Persians had defeated the Romans. The idolaters of Makkah favored the Persians, who were idol worshippers, while the Muslims favored the Romans because they were People of the Book. When the verses foretold that the Romans would be victorious within a few years, Abu Bakr proclaimed this in Makkah and made a wager with the idolaters over the outcome, which the Romans later fulfilled.
30:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

30:28.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that the idolaters used to say in their Talbiyah, declaring that Allah had no partner except a partner whom He owned along with whatever that partner owned. Allah then revealed this verse setting forth the parable that they would not accept their own servants as equal partners in their wealth, so how could they ascribe partners to Allah.
30:28.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:28.occasion: Revealed when the Prophet's wives asked him to increase their provision and maintenance. Allah commanded him to offer them the choice between the life of this world, in which case he would release them handsomely, or remaining with him desiring Allah, His Messenger and the Hereafter.
33:28.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:50.occasion: The portion concerning a believing woman who offers herself to the Prophet was connected by Aisha to Khawlah bint Hakim, who offered herself in marriage to the Prophet.
33:50.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:69.occasion: Connected to an incident in which a man criticized the Prophet's distribution of war booty as not being for the sake of Allah; the Prophet's face reddened and he said that Musa had been annoyed with worse than that yet remained patient.
33:69.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

39:53.occasion: Al-Bukhari recorded from Ibn 'Abbas that some idolators who had killed many people and committed much fornication came to the Prophet and said that what he was calling them to was good, if only he could tell them there was an expiation for what they had done. Then this verse, along with the verses of Surah Al-Furqan (25:68-70), was revealed.
39:53.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

41:22.occasion: Ibn Mas'ud reported that while he was hiding beneath the covering of the Ka'bah, three men with large bellies and little understanding (one from the Quraysh with two Thaqafi in-laws, or the reverse) wondered aloud whether Allah could hear their words, one saying He would hear only if they raised their voices. He mentioned this to the Prophet, and Allah revealed these verses about those who thought Allah did not know much of what they were doing.
41:22.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

43:57.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates that after the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited that they and what they worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell, 'Abdullah bin Az-Zab'ari argued contentiously that the Christians worship 'Isa, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and Quraysh worship the angels, so would they all be in the Fire. The Quraysh were delighted and clamored at this argument, and this verse was revealed concerning their disputatious objection to the mention of the son of Maryam.
43:57.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

47:33.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Abu al-Aliyah and from Ibn Umar that the Companions used to assume no sin would harm a person who professed La ilaha illallah, just as no good deed would benefit one who associated partners with Allah. Allah then revealed the command to obey Allah and the Messenger and not to invalidate one's deeds, which made them fear that some sins could nullify their good works.
47:33.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:11.occasion: This was revealed concerning the bedouins who lagged behind and did not set out with the Prophet for Al-Hudaybiyyah, preferring their possessions and families. They asked the Prophet to seek forgiveness for them, saying with their tongues what was not in their hearts.
48:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:15.occasion: This was revealed concerning those bedouins who had lagged behind at Al-Hudaybiyyah and then asked to accompany the Muslims to take the spoils of Khaybar. Allah commanded His Messenger to refuse them, since the spoils of Khaybar had been promised to those who were present at Al-Hudaybiyyah.
48:15.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:24.occasion: Anas bin Malik reported that on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah about eighty armed men came down from Mount At-Tan'im to ambush the Messenger of Allah; he invoked Allah against them and they were captured, then he pardoned them, and this verse was revealed concerning that incident.
48:24.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:26.occasion: This was revealed concerning the pride and haughtiness the disbelievers showed during the treaty negotiations at Al-Hudaybiyyah, when they refused to allow the words 'In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful' and 'Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah' to be written in the treaty document.
48:26.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:27.occasion: This was revealed concerning the true dream-vision Allah showed the Prophet of entering Makkah and performing Tawaf, which he told his Companions in Al-Madinah. When the Hudaybiyyah treaty forced them to return without entering Makkah that year, some Companions, including 'Umar, questioned this, and the verse confirmed the vision would be fulfilled.
48:27.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:2.occasion: It was stated that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Umar. When a delegation from Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (peace be upon him), the two of them differed over whom to recommend as its leader and raised their voices in his presence until their dispute grew loud, whereupon this verse was revealed.
49:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:17.occasion: Ibn Abbas related that Banu Asad came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we embraced Islam, and the Arabs fought you while we did not fight you,' counting their Islam as a favor to him. This verse was then revealed.
49:17.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

52:30.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that when the Quraysh gathered in their assembly hall (Dar An-Nadwah) to plot against the Prophet (peace be upon him), one of them proposed imprisoning him in chains and waiting for death to overtake him as it had earlier poets such as Zuhayr and An-Nabighah, claiming he was merely a poet like them. In response Allah revealed, 'Or do they say: A poet! We await for him some calamity by time!'
52:30.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

56:39.occasion: Abu Hurairah reported that when the verses 'A multitude of those will be from the first ones, and a few of those will be from the later ones' (56:13-14) were revealed, this was hard on the Companions of the Prophet. Then the verses 'A multitude of those will be from the first ones, and a multitude of those will be from the later ones' (56:39-40) were revealed, and the Prophet said he hoped they would be a quarter, then a third, then half of the people of Paradise.
56:39.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

58:1.occasion: Khawlah bint Tha'labah came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and disputed with him about her husband Aws bin As-Samit, who had pronounced Zihar against her (declaring her unlawful to him like his mother's back), complaining of how he had spent her wealth, exhausted her youth, and cast her off when she grew old. Aishah was in a corner of the room and could not hear all that she said, yet Allah heard her complaint and revealed this verse.
58:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

58:8.occasion: The Jews, who had a treaty with the Prophet (peace be upon him), would hold secret counsels when a Muslim passed by their gathering, making him fear they were plotting to harm him. Though warned to stop, they persisted, and this verse was revealed about them. They would also greet the Prophet by twisting the greeting into 'As-Sam alayka' (death be upon you), saying within themselves that Allah would have punished them if he were truly a Prophet.
58:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

58:12.occasion: The Muslims kept asking Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) so many questions that it became burdensome for him. To lighten this, Allah commanded that anyone wishing to consult the Prophet privately should first give charity. Many then refrained from such private talk, and only Ali bin Abi Talib is reported to have acted upon this command before it was abrogated by the following verse.
58:12.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

59:9.occasion: A poor man came to the Prophet complaining of hunger, and an Ansari (named in another narration as Abu Talhah) took him home; finding only food for the children, he and his wife put the children to sleep hungry and turned off the lamp so the guest could eat. The next morning the Prophet said Allah was pleased with their action, and this verse praising those who give others preference over themselves was revealed.
59:9.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

59:11.occasion: Ibn Kathir states that this passage was revealed about the hypocrites, such as Abdullah bin Ubayy and those like him, who sent word to Bani An-Nadir falsely promising that they would go out with them if they were expelled and help them if they were attacked, a promise they never intended to keep.
59:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

60:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir states the opening of the surah was revealed concerning Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) prepared to march on Makkah, Hatib secretly sent a letter with a woman warning the Quraysh of the planned attack, hoping they would protect his family there. The Prophet was informed, the letter was intercepted, and Hatib's excuse was accepted, after which these verses came down.
60:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

60:8.occasion: Asma' bint Abi Bakr's mother Qutaylah, who was still an idolatress, came to her with gifts during the period of the treaty with Quraysh. Asma' refused to receive her or accept the gifts and asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) through 'A'ishah, whereupon this verse was revealed permitting kind and just treatment of disbelievers who do not fight the believers over religion, and the Prophet ordered her to receive her mother.
60:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

61:10.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Abdullah bin Salam that the Companions wished to ask the Prophet (peace be upon him) about the deeds most beloved to Allah so they could practice them, and Allah sent down this Surah, including this verse inviting them to the trade that saves from a painful torment.
61:10.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

62:3.occasion: While the Companions were sitting with the Prophet (peace be upon him) and Surat Al-Jumu'ah was revealed, they asked who was meant by 'And others among them who have not yet joined them.' He did not answer until they had asked three times, then he placed his hand on Salman Al-Farisi and said that even if faith were as far as the Pleiades, men or a man from his people would attain it.
62:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

62:11.occasion: A trading caravan arrived in Al-Madinah while the Prophet (peace be upon him) was standing delivering the Friday sermon, and the people rushed out to it for the merchandise, leaving only about twelve men with him. This verse was then sent down rebuking that behavior.
62:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

64:14.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn 'Abbas that some men in Makkah embraced Islam and wished to migrate to the Messenger of Allah, but their wives and children refused to let them go. When they later joined the Prophet and saw that the Companions had gained understanding of the religion, they were about to punish their wives and children, so Allah revealed the words 'But if you pardon and overlook, and forgive, then verily, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.'
64:14.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

65:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Al-Bukhari that Abdullah bin Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the lifetime of the Prophet (peace be upon him). When Umar bin Al-Khattab mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah, he became angry and ordered that Ibn Umar take her back and wait until she was pure before divorcing her, then recited this verse about divorcing women at their prescribed period.
65:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

66:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from 'A'ishah (recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to drink honey at the house of one of his wives. Out of jealousy, 'A'ishah and Hafsah agreed to tell him that they smelled Maghafir on him, so he vowed to never drink the honey again and asked that this be kept secret. These verses were then revealed, censuring him for forbidding to himself what Allah had made lawful and addressing the two wives who were to turn in repentance.
66:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

66:3.occasion: Ibn Kathir explains that the secret the Prophet (peace be upon him) confidentially disclosed to one of his wives was his statement that he had drunk honey and would not drink it again, together with his instruction not to tell anyone. When she disclosed it, Allah informed him of it, which is the occasion of this verse.
66:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

66:5.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Anas (recorded by al-Bukhari) that 'Umar, when the Prophet's wives were jealously pressing him, said to them the very words, 'Maybe his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him instead of you wives better than you,' after which this verse was revealed. Ibn Kathir adds that the wife who rebuked 'Umar for interfering was Umm Salamah.
66:5.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

73:1.occasion: According to the report of A'ishah, Allah made standing in night prayer obligatory at the beginning of this Surah, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and his Companions stood praying for an entire year until their feet swelled. Allah withheld the end of the Surah for twelve months and then revealed the lightening of this obligation at its close.
73:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

74:1.occasion: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah prepared food for the Quraysh, and afterward they debated what to call the Prophet (peace be upon him), some saying magician, soothsayer, or poet, until they agreed to call it 'magic from of old.' When this reached the Prophet he became grieved and covered and wrapped himself, whereupon Allah revealed these verses.
74:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

75:34.occasion: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took hold of Abu Jahl and said to him, "Woe to you, and then woe to you! Again woe to you, and then woe to you!" Allah then revealed this verse.
75:34.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

93:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that the Prophet (peace be upon him) became ill and did not stand for prayer for a night or two, after which a woman said to him, 'O Muhammad, I think your devil has finally left you.' In another narration, the revelation came when Jibril was delayed in coming to the Prophet for a number of days, and the idolaters began saying that his Lord had forsaken and hated him. So Allah revealed these opening verses.
93:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

96:1.occasion: These were the very first verses of the Qur'an to be revealed. While the Prophet (peace be upon him) was secluded in the cave of Hira, the angel came to him and commanded him to read. When he answered that he was not one who reads, the angel pressed him and then recited these opening verses, marking the beginning of his prophethood.
96:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

99:7.occasion: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked about donkeys, he replied that Allah had revealed nothing concerning them except this single, comprehensive verse, that whoever does an atom's weight of good or evil shall see it.
99:7.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

102:1.occasion: Ubayy bin Ka'b reported that the Companions used to regard the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him), 'If the Son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would desire another like it,' as part of the Qur'an, until this verse (At-Takathur) was revealed.
102:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

109:1.occasion: It has been related that the disbelievers of the Quraysh, in their ignorance, invited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) to worship their idols for a year on the condition that they would worship his God for a year. In response Allah revealed this Surah, commanding His Messenger to disavow himself completely from their religion.
109:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim
